headline: Analytic-choice sensitivity and resampling stability tests in omics analyses
label: Reproducible Computational Omics Methods
summary: Preprocessing and analytic choices alter feature shortlists and partitions, prompting auditable reproducibility checks built into analysis pipelines.
synthesis: The shared thread is treating reproducibility as an explicit analytic component rather than a final check. The untargeted LC-MS pipeline uses a multiverse-consensus design to make feature selection auditable, reporting that preprocessing decisions alter feature shortlists. The label-free multi-metric single-cell RNA-seq pipeline benchmarks clustering and tests whether cell-type heterogeneity holds under bootstrap and re-embedding, with the stated ability to distinguish real bipolar sub-structure. The MIMIC-IV preprint is a clinical-prediction study rather than an omics study, but it follows the same logic: it audits recording artifacts before comparing bounded and full fine-tuning of ICU prediction models under drift gating. What is new across these items is the explicit coupling of audit and sensitivity testing to the analysis itself.
